text:
AcmeApp: hey team — started seeing p99 jump to ~3.5s on /v1/generate for our tenant since 2026-03-16 10:12 UTC. Affects only our traffic, p95 ~200ms unchanged. also noticed intermittent 503s. request id sample: req_9a1b2c. can you look?

emma.support: thanks—sorry you hit this. can you paste a sample curl and confirm region? also asking if you made any config changes on your side.

AcmeApp: curl below, region eu-west-1. no changes on our side. we did see a small increase in QPS but within usual.
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-acme..." \
  -d '{"model":"rw-large", "input":"short prompt"}'
```

li.eng-sre: looking. curious: p95 stable, p99 up — classic tail due to batching or auth retries. did we roll anything last night? rafi?

rafi.eng-platform: we rolled continuous-batcher default tuning at 02:00 UTC: increased default `hold_window_ms` from 15 -> 50 to improve throughput on high-latency models. rollout targeted hosted pool but some tenant-level overrides might've been bumped.

li.eng-sre: that matches. increasing hold window can widen tail for tiny prompts. can you share a few request traces / logs for req_9a1b2c? also check token refresh logs — if auth refresh blocks a worker it can force request into a later batch.

AcmeApp: attaching trace id trace_77ee (copied logs).
```
[trace_77ee] 10:12:03 recv req req_9a1b2c size=48
[trace_77ee] 10:12:03 enqueue tenant=acme hold_window=50ms batch_id=114
[trace_77ee] 10:12:03 auth: token ok
[trace_77ee] 10:12:06 dispatch batch_id=114 latency=3090ms p99
```

emma.support: ok logs show hold_window=50ms and dispatch delay long (~3s). also saw one auth retry earlier for a different req which timed out and got 503 — requeues add jitter.

zach.oncall: immediate mitigation options: 1) per-tenant override drop `hold_window_ms` to 10ms for acme tenant; 2) pin tenant to `force_single` (bypass continuous batching); 3) rollback global change (risky). i'd prefer 1 then 2 if needed. can engineering apply override quickly?

rafi.eng-platform: we can push per-tenant override via control-plane CLI. run: 
```
redwoodctl tenants update acme --set continuous_batcher.hold_window_ms=10
```
will apply within ~30s to hosts in-control-plane. want me to run?

emma.support: please run and tell customer we're trying a config tweak. i'll update Acme.

rafi.eng-platform: running now...

deploy-bot: started tenant-config-update acme id=cfg-20260316-01 status=IN_PROGRESS

deploy-bot: completed tenant-config-update acme id=cfg-20260316-01 status=SUCCEEDED in 18s

li.eng-sre: can we get post-change traces? Acme, any immediate change in observed latency?

AcmeApp: after your change p95 ~190ms, p99 dropped to ~1.1s — much better but still above baseline. we still see occasional 503s (~0.02% requests).

li.eng-sre: good improvement. remaining p99 ~1.1s suggests another source: auth retries or billing/auth proxy slow path. can you confirm the 503s correlate with `auth: timeout` in logs?

AcmeApp: one of the 503 traces shows `auth refresh failed: 504` then request retried.

zach.oncall: that explains residual tail. sequence: longer hold window increased probability that auth refresh or token expiry occurs mid-queue → requeue/tie up subsequent batches. mitigation: 1) short-term keep hold window low for this tenant; 2) add an early auth check path that rejects fast on expired token instead of retrying; 3) we can force `force_single` for more safety if they still see 503s.

emma.support: i'll propose two-step plan to Acme: (A) keep new hold_window=10ms for 24h and monitor; (B) if they still see any error spikes, we'll flip `batch_policy=force_single` for them for a limited window while platform team ships auth-refresh hardening. ok?

rafi.eng-platform: ack. prepping `force_single` flip command:
```
redwoodctl tenants update acme --set batch_policy=force_single
```
note: this increases per-token cost for tenant and reduces throughput but should eliminate batch tail amplification.

li.eng-sre: also adding a short-term observability check: create a saved query: `auth_refresh_failures by tenant 1m` and an alert if rate > 0.1% for acme. i'll create and link.

deploy-bot: saved-query created id=q-20260316-auth-acme

emma.support: thanks. acme — i'll post these changes and the mitigation plan in your ticket and offer the `force_single` flip if needed. any other asks?

AcmeApp: appreciate the quick response. please keep us updated.

zach.oncall: followups for eng: 1) can eng-platform add a canary rule so future `hold_window` rollouts exclude tenants with recent auth-retry history? 2) consider decoupling auth refresh from batch critical path (fast-fail).

rafi.eng-platform: noted — i'll open a small follow-up RFC for rollout guard and an immediate canary exclude list.

li.eng-sre: i'll keep the alert on and monitor p99. thanks all. :thumbsup:
